title: Understanding Your Rights
learning_goal: Learn about legal, safety, and personal rights for people experiencing DFV.

content.micro_lesson: Everyone has the right to safety, autonomy, privacy, and freedom from violence. DFV laws protect victims through intervention orders, police responses, and child safety frameworks.
content.activity: Identify three rights that apply to your situation and explain why they matter.
content.caseworker_flags: Learner expresses belief they have 'no rights' or cannot seek help.
content.escalation_trigger: Disclosure of blocked access to legal protections triggers urgent triage.

title: Building a Support Network
learning_goal: Identify safe people and services that can provide emotional or practical support.

content.micro_lesson: Support networks may include friends, family, neighbours, caseworkers, IDVAs, counsellors, and community groups. Safe support reduces isolation and increases safety.
content.activity: Create a support network map using the template.
content.caseworker_flags: Learner reports having no safe contacts.
content.escalation_trigger: Total isolation or blocked communication triggers immediate safety review.

title: Healthy Boundaries
learning_goal: Understand what healthy boundaries look like and how to set them safely.

content.micro_lesson: Boundaries protect emotional and physical wellbeing. Examples include limits on communication, privacy, personal space, and emotional labour.
content.activity: Write three boundaries you want to set and identify potential risks.
content.caseworker_flags: Learner expresses fear of retaliation for setting boundaries.
content.escalation_trigger: Any boundary-setting attempt that triggers threats requires immediate triage.

title: Emotional Regulation
learning_goal: Learn grounding and regulation techniques to manage stress and trauma responses.

content.micro_lesson: Trauma affects the nervous system. Regulation tools include breathing exercises, grounding, sensory resets, and self-compassion practices.
content.activity: Complete a 5-minute grounding exercise and reflect on the experience.
content.caseworker_flags: Learner reports panic attacks or inability to regulate emotions.
content.escalation_trigger: Severe dysregulation or dissociation triggers clinical referral.

title: Help-Seeking Pathways
learning_goal: Understand how to access professional support safely and effectively.

content.micro_lesson: Help-seeking includes contacting DFV services, IDVAs, police, legal aid, housing services, and counselling. Safety considerations include timing, privacy, and technology safety.
content.activity: Identify two services you may need and outline how you would contact them safely.
content.caseworker_flags: Learner reports being blocked from contacting services.
content.escalation_trigger: Any interference with help-seeking triggers urgent safety intervention.

title: Rebuilding Confidence
learning_goal: Recognise strengths and rebuild self-worth after DFV.

content.micro_lesson: DFV erodes confidence through criticism, control, and isolation. Rebuilding involves recognising strengths, achievements, and personal values.
content.caseworker_flags: Learner expresses extreme self-blame or hopelessness.
content.escalation_trigger: Statements indicating inability to function or care for children trigger triage.

title: Reflection & Next Steps
learning_goal: Consolidate Week 4 learning and identify next steps for safety and wellbeing.

content.micro_lesson: This lesson reviews rights, boundaries, support networks, and emotional regulation. Learners identify one action to take in the next week.
content.activity: Write a 200-word reflection and choose one next-step action.
content.caseworker_flags: Learner reports worsening risk or new threats.
content.escalation_trigger: Any new high-risk disclosure triggers immediate safety response.
